thread:
maria.g: Heads-up — last 60m we saw eu-west GPU pools spike and a large number of SDK retries which in turn amplified 429s. Proposal: add a lightweight "admission-resume" token header so SDKs can do cheap probes instead of aggressive retry storms.

ashok: Can you paste a sample header and how it's supposed to behave? Are we reusing Retry-After or inventing a new header?

maria.g: Sample (server -> client):
```
X-RW-Admission-Resume: v1:eyJ0b2tlbiI6Ij...
X-RW-Queue-Bucket: 75
X-RW-Resume-TTL: 5  # seconds
```
Semantics: token is opaque to clients, short TTL (5s). Client may send a single probe request carrying `X-RW-Admission-Resume` to check if capacity freed without entering full queue. If probe accepted, server returns 200; if still full, 429 + optional Retry-After.

kevin: How does this play with the shedder and admission queue? If a probe is accepted do we allocate a slot immediately or hand it a short-lived 'fast-path' slot?

maria.g: Fast-path: acceptance means we can push the request into a preemptive ephemeral slot for a single RPC. No long-lived admit. If the request is heavier than expected, it falls back to normal admission. This avoids requeuing many clients.

olivia: +1 but we need client-side limits. SDKs must cap probes per client-id (eg: 3 probes per 30s) and always apply jitter. Also recommend default probe interval > 800ms to avoid synchronized bursts.

maria.g: Agreed. Recommended SDK behavior: on 429 -> stop exponential retries. Instead: do a single probe after a random delay in [800ms, 1500ms]. If probe fails, escalate backoff exponentially but keep probe path for occasional checks. Respect `Retry-After` if present.

ashok: What about older SDKs that ignore the header? They may keep hammering. Any server-side protections?

kevin: We'll keep the 429 semantics unchanged for compatibility. Header is opt-in for clients that implement probe flow. On server side we also want admission token rate-limiter per client-ip/tenant to prevent abuse.

olivia: Regarding `X-RW-Queue-Bucket`, I don't want to leak exact queue sizes. Use coarse buckets only (0,25,50,75,100). That gives enough signal without exposing backend telemetry.

deploy-bot: scheduled: rollout/admission-resume canary -> eu-west, 2026-03-24T09:00:00Z (canary window 2h)

maria.g: TL;DR for SDK team: new header `X-RW-Admission-Resume`, coarse `X-RW-Queue-Bucket`, and `X-RW-Resume-TTL`. SDKs should: 1) switch from aggressive exp-retry to probe-and-pause, 2) apply jitter and per-client probe caps, 3) fall back to existing 429 behavior if header absent.

ashok: I'll draft the SDK spec and add examples + pseudo-code for probe flow. Also adding telemetry hooks: `resume_probe_sent`, `resume_probe_accepted`, `resume_probe_rejected`.

kevin: Add runtime metrics server-side too: `resume_token_issued`, `resume_token_consumed`, `resume_token_rejected`, and a counter for token-issuance-per-tenant (rate-limited). Make sure tokens are HMACed per-region so they can't be reused cross-region.

olivia: Security note: tokens should not contain any PII, be signed, short expiry, and for private deployments allow a config toggle to disable tokens. I'll write a short blurb for the compliance doc.

maria.g: Great. I'll own the server PR for token generation + coarse-bucket logic. @ashok please own the SDK spec and sample change log. We'll canary in eu-west tomorrow and report metrics here. :thumbsup:

kevin: +1 — once canary metrics look good we can extend to other regions.

ashok: Copy that, will start the spec draft now and tag you both when ready.
